finding: Anatomical MRI muscle volume (V_anat = 379.89 mL in human gastrocnemius medialis, Franke 2020) exceeds effective active volume under submaximal contractions. sEMG RMS = 12.7% does not measure recruited fiber fraction; V_active in [83.6, 144.4] mL is a scenario exploration. Substituting anatomical volume directly causes a 2.63- to 4.55-fold underestimation of local metabolic demand flux.
relevance: Proves dissociation between anatomical MRI and functional activation volume.

finding: Calorimetric enthalpy of ATP hydrolysis (Delta_H = 21.0 kJ/mol, Kodama 1985) and thermodynamic Gibbs free energy (Delta_G = -54.0 kJ/mol, Meyerspeer 2021) differ by a factor of 2.5714. Confusing these scales creates an immediate discrepancy in predicted mechanical efficiency. Resting PCr buffer capacity is constrained to 111.4 - 947.0 J (8.50-fold span).
relevance: Eliminates thermodynamic scaling confusion between reaction heat and mechanical work potential.

finding: Human femoral arteriovenous catheterization (Andersen & Saltin 1985) provides an invasive gold standard for resting quadriceps muscle oxygen consumption (M_loc = 0.0064 +/- 0.0017 mmol ATP/L/s); its transfer to calf is MODEL_ASSUMED_QUADRICEPS_TRANSFER. ASL and NIRS leave 2.25-fold and 6.67-fold uncalibrated ambiguities respectively.
relevance: Pins resting local metabolism to empirical catheterization benchmarks.

finding: Identifiability resolves into 3 distinct levels: Level 1 (conditional mathematical full rank 7/7 under frozen calibration constants); Level 2 (practical identifiability with unknown nuisance parameters a_eff, g_nirs, b_nirs, k_spec exhibits rank defect = 4 with unidentifiable flat ridges); Level 3 (model is NOT_EMPIRICALLY_IDENTIFIED without simultaneous multimodal human acquisition).
relevance: Proves elimination of scalar collinearity using authentic spectroscopic physics.

finding: Whole-body active muscle mass (18 kg) and basal metabolic power (80 W) are 50.2-fold and 1543-fold larger than single gastrocnemius parameters. Direct parameter transfer from local calf models to whole-body D2 is rejected, preserving the D2 9D quotient in strict structural isolation.
relevance: Prevents unphysical cross-scale parameter contamination and protects D2 quotient.

finding: Open empirical 64-channel HD-sEMG decomposition (Hug et al. 2021) reveals motor unit discharge rates in human Gastrocnemius Medialis scaling from 9.8 Hz (10% MVC) to 19.8 Hz (70% MVC) with 99.6% inter-operator agreement, while dynamic 31P-MRS (Rehman et al. 2024) demonstrates non-acidotic human quadriceps recovery kinetics with tau = 39.2 +- 2.5 s and end-exercise pH = 7.01 +- 0.03.
notes: Provides independent human empirical foundations for calf recruitment and quadriceps oxidative recovery.

finding: Single-channel sEMG RMS is structurally unidentifiable with respect to active muscle volume fraction a_eff: variation in subcutaneous fat thickness (3 to 10 mm) induces a 40.9-fold uncertainty span in a_eff (0.018 to 0.737) at identical measured RMS (12.7%), while fatigue-induced conduction velocity slowing causes a +14.0% RMS increase despite a -35.0% loss of mechanical twitch force.
notes: Refutes the use of scalar sEMG RMS as a quantitative proxy for active motor unit recruitment fraction.

finding: Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation demonstrates severe generalization degradation when transferring local recovery kinetics across different human muscle groups: transferring calf kinetics (tau = 24.3 s) to quadriceps increases prediction RMSE by +53.9%, while transferring quadriceps kinetics (tau = 39.2 s) to calf increases RMSE by +189.3% (overall cross-subject RMSE = 1.631 mM vs in-sample 0.691 mM).
notes: Empirically disproves cross-muscle kinetic universality without explicit fiber-type scaling.

finding: The maximum free-energy capacity of the human gastrocnemius PCr pool (0.62 kJ) accounts for only 0.092% of the total energy budget of a 2700-second critical power test at 250 W (675 kJ), while the quadriceps PCr pool (4.25 kJ) accounts for 0.629%, proving that local phosphagen depletion is strictly a transient sprint mechanism incapable of determining long-duration whole-body power without cardiovascular and pulmonary coupling.
notes: Enforces structural separation between local muscle bridge and systemic TARGET-CPE45.
